symbols.name: ServiceCollectionExtensions
symbols.summary: Provides dependency-injection registration for Requester and Notifier services and behaviors.

symbols.name: AddRequester(IServiceCollection)
symbols.summary: Adds the Requester service to the specified Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.IServiceCollection and returns a BridgingIT.DevKit.Common.RequesterBuilder for configuration.
symbols.remarks: This method registers the necessary services for the Requester system, including the BridgingIT.DevKit.Common.IRequester implementation and its dependencies. It returns a BridgingIT.DevKit.Common.RequesterBuilder that can be used to configure handlers and behaviors using a fluent API. The Requester system enables dispatching requests to their corresponding handlers through a pipeline of behaviors, supporting features like validation, retry, timeout, and chaos injection. To use the Requester system, you must: 1. Call BridgingIT.DevKit.Common.ServiceCollectionExtensions.AddRequester(Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.IServiceCollection) to register the core services. 2. Use BridgingIT.DevKit.Common.RequesterBuilder.AddHandlers(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable%7bSystem.String%7d) to scan for and register request handlers. 3. Optionally, use BridgingIT.DevKit.Common.RequesterBuilder.WithBehavior(System.Type) to add pipeline behaviors. 4. Build the service provider to resolve the BridgingIT.DevKit.Common.IRequester service for dispatching requests. The BridgingIT.DevKit.Common.IRequester service is registered with a scoped lifetime, meaning a new instance is created for each scope (e.g., per HTTP request in ASP.NET Core). Ensure that any dependencies (e.g., logging) are also registered in the service collection before calling this method.

syntax.content: public static RequesterBuilder AddRequester(this IServiceCollection services)

symbols.name: AddNotifier(IServiceCollection)
symbols.summary: Adds the Notifier service to the specified Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.IServiceCollection and returns a BridgingIT.DevKit.Common.NotifierBuilder for configuration.
symbols.remarks: This method registers the necessary services for the Notifier system, including the BridgingIT.DevKit.Common.INotifier implementation and its dependencies. It returns a BridgingIT.DevKit.Common.NotifierBuilder that can be used to configure handlers and behaviors using a fluent API. The Notifier system enables dispatching notifications to their corresponding handlers through a pipeline of behaviors, supporting features like validation, retry, and timeout. To use the Notifier system, you must: 1. Call BridgingIT.DevKit.Common.ServiceCollectionExtensions.AddNotifier(Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.IServiceCollection) to register the core services. 2. Use BridgingIT.DevKit.Common.NotifierBuilder.AddHandlers(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable%7bSystem.String%7d) to scan for and register notification handlers. 3. Optionally, use BridgingIT.DevKit.Common.NotifierBuilder.WithBehavior(System.Type) to add pipeline behaviors. 4. Build the service provider to resolve the BridgingIT.DevKit.Common.INotifier service for dispatching notifications. The BridgingIT.DevKit.Common.INotifier service is registered with a scoped lifetime, meaning a new instance is created for each scope (e.g., per HTTP request in ASP.NET Core). Ensure that any dependencies (e.g., logging) are also registered in the service collection before calling this method.
